tone_statements.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 1972. A Phonological Study of Fe'fe'-Bamileke. Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 4. Los Angeles: UCLA. xii+230 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Surface forms in Fe'fe' can carry any one of four discrete level tones, or a contour tone (either rising or falling). The following four forms, contrasting only in tone, were given in Chapter II: (2) Low (`) : [pʉ̀ɑ] 'bag' Raised-Low (') : [pʉ'ɑ] 'to bend over' Mid ( ) : [pʉɑ] 'to go crazy' High (´) : [pʉ́ɑ] 'two' [...] The symbols used are the grave accent (`) for low tone, an apostrophe (') for raised-low tone, a macron (¯) or usually no mark for mid tone, and an acute accent (´) for high tone. These four simple tones are the same as those recognized by Stoll [1955] and Ngangoum [1970], although the terminology differs.
tone_statements.locator: p.129-130, Chapter VI 'Tone', sec. 1.0 'The Phonetic Tones of Fe'fe''
tone_statements.n_tones: 4 level (L, raised-L, M, H) + 4 contour (rising 'M, 'H; falling M-L, H-L)

sources.note: Secondhand via Hyman 1972:127-130 and Ngangoum 2015:23: first tonal description of Fe'fe'; recognizes the same four surface tones as Hyman but rejects 'mid tone' - a low tone, a 'high' (= Hyman's mid), a raised low 'sous-dominante' (= raised-low) and a raised high 'dominante' (= high), in a 'système de la double symétrie'; also tone-symbolism speculation and noun-class tone. Hyman calls the Fe'fe' analysis 'very reliable'.
